diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that $\Matrix{B}^\pinv \Matrix{B} = \Matrix{I}_{m}$ and $\Matrix{C} \Matrix{C}^\pinv = \Matrix{I}_{n}$, then substitute $\Matrix{C}^\pinv \Batrix{A}^\pinv \Matrix{B}^\pinv$ into Theorem~\ref{theorem:pinv_bochner}.

issues.failure_explanation: Part 2 asserts (BAC)^† = C^†A^†B^† whenever B has full column rank and C has full row rank. Only B^†B = I and CC^† = I are used. These give the first two Penrose equations but not the two Hermitian conditions, so the substitution does not prove the claim. Counterexample with H = F: A = diag(1,0), B = [[1,0],[1,1]], C = I. Then BA = [1;1][1,0], so (BA)^† = [[1/2,1/2],[0,0]], while A^†B^† = [[1,0],[0,0]]. The identity holds in general only when B has orthonormal columns and C has orthonormal rows.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the hypothesis by 'B has orthonormal columns and C has orthonormal rows' and check all four Penrose conditions directly. Alternatively, restrict the statement to full-rank factorizations.
issues.overall_effect: Part 2 of the lemma is false as stated, even for usual matrices. No later result in the paper uses it; the CUR lemma uses only the full-rank-factorization identity (FG)^† = G^†F^†, which is valid.
issues.title: Pseudoinverse product rule claimed for arbitrary full-rank B, C is false
issues.why_classification: A local change of hypothesis with a short direct verification repairs it, and nothing downstream depends on the general form.

issues.failure_explanation: H may be infinite-dimensional, so H^{m×n} is not locally compact. A closed set in such a space need not contain a nearest point to a given element. The proof infers existence of a minimizer C_* from closedness alone. Existence needs a further argument, for example projecting any competitor onto the finite-dimensional span of stock(A) without increasing the error or the Tucker rank, and then using compactness there.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the final bound with an infimum. The proof then works for every C in the set without needing a minimizer. Alternatively, add the short reduction to the finite-dimensional span of stock(A).

issues.title: Existence of a minimizer in an infinite-dimensional space deduced from closedness alone
issues.why_classification: The bound holds for each competitor, so replacing min by inf or adding a short projection argument keeps the sqrt(2) quasi-optimality.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims the solution of -u'' - α²u = cos(βx), u(0)=u(π)=0 has sine coefficients with denominator (k²+α²)(k²+β²). The operator -d²/dx² - α² acts on sin(kx) as multiplication by k²-α². Also ∫_0^π cos(βx) sin(kx) dx = k[1-(-1)^k cos(βπ)]/(k²-β²). The correct denominator is therefore (k²-α²)(k²-β²), which vanishes at integer α or β. The formula as given corresponds to a different problem, so the data generating the Bochner matrix in the experiment are not the solutions of the stated equation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either change the ODE to match the formula (for example -u'' + α²u with an appropriate right-hand side) or correct the denominators to (k²-α²)(k²-β²). Then confirm that the chosen parameter ranges avoid resonance, or rerun the experiment.
issues.overall_effect: The first experiment's solution map is mis-specified relative to the stated ODE. The reported errors are for the formula's data, not for the stated problem. Near-resonance behaviour at α, β near 1 and 2 would differ if the ODE were taken as stated.
issues.title: Stated Fourier-coefficient formula does not solve the stated boundary-value problem
issues.why_classification: It is a local correction in the numerical section with no effect on any theorem. The method and conclusions are unchanged, though the experiment may need to be rerun.
